policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads simply "I charge thee in the sight of God" with no inferential connective or emphatic pronoun; the RP expansion adds oun ego ("I therefore"), which the ASV would render "I charge thee therefore". The absent "therefore" distinguishes the shorter base reading.
ASV has "and of Christ Jesus". The RP reading tou kuriou Iesou Christou would give "the Lord Jesus Christ"; the ASV supplies no "Lord" here and keeps the order Christ Jesus, matching the base lemma.

ASV "and by his appearing and his kingdom" renders the connective kai with the accusative of adjuration ("and by"), and the mapped alternative rendering "both of his appearing etc." likewise presupposes kai...kai. The RP preposition kata would give "at" or "according to his appearing", which the ASV nowhere reflects.

The variant is only the position of idias relative to epithumias; both yield "after their own lusts". ASV word order in English cannot distinguish Greek attributive order, and no note is mapped here (the two notes concern "healthful" and "teaching").
Possessive genitive mou versus the attributive adjective emes; both are rendered "my departure". ASV offers no wording or note that would separate the two constructions.
Attributive order only: kalon agona versus agona ton kalon, both "the good fight" in ASV. English cannot register the difference and no note is attached to the verse.

The two forms differ only by the itacistic spelling of the stem vowel (-lip-/-leip-). ASV "Demas forsook me" is compatible with either printed spelling; the mapped notes concern "age" and "Gaul", not this unit.
An itacistic spelling difference (apelipon / apeleipon). ASV "The cloak that I left at Troas" reflects either form; the verse carries no note.

ASV "the Lord will render to him according to his works" is a future indicative statement. The RP optative apodoie would be a wish, "may the Lord render" (compare the ASV's own optative rendering "may it not be laid to their account" in v. 16). The indicative future distinguishes the base reading.

ASV "he greatly withstood our words" is a simple past answering the aorist anteste. The ASV renders the Greek perfect with "hath" plus participle, so the RP perfect anthesteken would have produced "hath greatly withstood". The tense of the English verb distinguishes the base reading.

ASV "no one took my part" renders the sense of standing with the speaker, which both the simple paregeneto and the compound sumparegeneto carry; the sun- prefix is already implicit in "took my part" and leaves no separate English word. Nothing in the verse or its notes selects between them.
Itacistic spelling only (enkatelipon / enkateleipon). ASV "all forsook me" is compatible with either printed form.

The variant is verbal number after the neuter plural subject panta ta ethne, which regularly takes either a plural or a singular verb in Greek. ASV "that all the Gentiles might hear" translates the plural subject and cannot show which verb form stood; the mapped notes concern "gave me power" and "proclamation".

ASV begins the sentence "The Lord will deliver me from every evil work" with no connective, while the RP reading prefixes kai, which the ASV renders as "And" when it stands at the head of a sentence. The absent "And" distinguishes the base reading.
Itacistic spelling only (apelipon / apeleipon). ASV "Trophimus I left at Miletus sick" reflects either form.
ASV "The Lord be with thy spirit" has no words answering the RP addition Iesous Christos, which the ASV would render "Jesus Christ". The bare "The Lord" distinguishes the base reading.
ASV ends the epistle "Grace be with you." with no "Amen", which the ASV prints wherever it renders Amen (as at 4:18). The absence of the closing Amen distinguishes the base reading.
